facts.fact: The World Bank assessment lists DHIS2 as the health ministry's (MSPLS) national platform for the routine data of the health system, with the ministry's Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire in charge of sector data; no date is given, so the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment states that DHIS2 is used in all provinces, with data entered at health centres (CDS) and at hospitals and analysed quarterly on the platform at district and provincial level; no date is given, so the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment states that facilities still record data by hand in standard paper registers, and that entry into DHIS2 is then done at the facility: by the deputy head of the health centre, who alone is allowed to key it, and by the hospital information officer directly in DHIS2; no date is given, so the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment gives no count or share of health centres keying their own reports; it gives report completeness in DHIS2 of more than 95% for health centres and 68% for hospitals, and timeliness of 40 to 60%, citing the UGADS progress report at 30 June 2022.

The World Bank assessment, citing PROGISSA, states that 41 of 71 public and faith-based hospitals are computerised (patient health records, facility management and automatic reporting), 39 of the 41 on OpenClinic, with nine more waiting; they are not interconnected and each has its own patient identifier; no date is given, so the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment states that six health centres (CDS) are computerised under a pilot financed by Enabel, with 29 more financed by Enabel and four by the government planned during 2023; no denominator of health centres is given, and the report's date is used.
The World Bank assessment lists OpenClinic under Enabel and the health ministry's PROGISSA, the health informatics programme the ministry created in 2020; the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment states that hospitals have been computerised with OpenClinic since 2014 under Enabel's PAISS project and that computerising the remaining hospitals depends on mobilising partner funds; the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment states that the government has begun contributing its own funds to computerising health facilities, with four health centres to be computerised on government financing during 2023; no budget line or amount is given, and the report's date is used.

The World Bank assessment lists the existence of a plan for computerising health facilities with OpenClinic as a strength, and cites the PNDIS II 2020-2024 as recommending the interconnection of care facilities and a national health data centre; the report's date is used.

systems.country_label: DHIS2, plateforme nationale du système national d'information sanitaire
systems.owner: MSPLS (Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire)
systems.tiers: all provinces; health centres (CDS), hospitals, health districts and provinces; also holds community and routine surveillance data

systems.country_label: Open Clinic, système de gestion des données hospitalières et des centres de santé
systems.tiers: 39 of the 41 computerised hospitals (of 71), almost all provinces; six pilot health centres

systems.country_label: Quick Soft, système de gestion des données hospitalières

systems.tiers: all provinces; performance-based financing and free-care data

systems.country_label: GMAO, gestion de la maintenance assistée par ordinateur
systems.tiers: districts of Kirundo, Muramvya, Bujumbura and Rumonge, extension under way since 2022
almost all health facilities; medical record of people living with HIV
laboratories of CHUK, INSP and the hospitals of Rumonge, Makamba, Kayanza and Muyinga; no longer functional in most except CHUK

systems.country_label: Système Informatisé d'Alerte et de Riposte Précoce aux Épidémies (SIARP)
systems.tiers: central; Covid-19 data from points of entry
points of entry, on tablets, for Covid-19 traveller registration

systems.country_label: Surveillance Intégrée des Maladies et Riposte (SMIR/SIMR)
systems.platform: SMS and email from private phones, then paper reports
systems.tiers: whole health system, 12 diseases under surveillance
community health workers in Gitega and Cankuzo provinces, since 2017

systems.platform: USSD and web application (MediaBox), interfaced with DHIS2
systems.tiers: community health workers around a few health centres, since late 2021; in test

systems.tiers: community health workers in Karusi and Makamba provinces

note: Community systems are stated as partner-led without effective ministry ownership; only the ICCM inputs application is stated as interfaced with the national DHIS2. The report does not say whether OpenClinic records are entered at the point of care, and it scores Burundi's digital health maturity at 1.5 of 5.
